$schema-note: Checked by `vp run suppressions:verify` (scripts/verify-suppressions.mjs). Read docs/agents/public-package-suppressions.md before touching this file.

policy.packages: Resolved at runtime from the workspaces that gitignore eslint-suppressions.json — the authority AGENTS.md names. Not listed here, so a fifth public package is covered the day it is added.
policy.rule: A suppression inside a public package is a defect until argued otherwise. Adding an entry here is not paperwork for a decision already made — it IS the decision, and it needs a reviewer who agrees.

status.required-on: Every entry in `approved`, and only those. A missing status, or one outside the two values below, fails the gate naming the entry (#514) — otherwise deleting the line silenced a suppression more cheaply than discharging it. Entries in `acknowledged` carry no status by design; see `lists.acknowledged`.
status.permanent: The engine is wrong about correct code and no fix exists in our control. Expected to outlive us.
status.provisional: Accepted for now, not endorsed — and it FAILS the gate (#510). Valid vocabulary inside one PR while a decision is open; discharge it before pushing, either by fixing the finding and deleting the entry or by restating it as permanent with a reason. It can never survive a build.

lists.approved: Suppressions scoped to a public package — the rule is off BECAUSE of that package. Highest bar: argue why the engine is wrong about this specific code, and declare a `status`.
lists.acknowledged: Repo-wide policy (ADR-035 §7) that happens to reach a public package, because the package contains a test file, a config, or a tooling script. These are decisions about a file CATEGORY, not about the package. Listed rather than justified per-package — but listed, so a new override cannot widen onto these packages unnoticed. No `status`: the package never chose these, so there is no per-package deferral to declare.

acknowledged.reason: The same config-module contract for eslint.config.mjs, which every public package owns.
A config module's entire contract IS its default export — Vite and Vitest load it that way. Reaches each public package through its own vite.config.ts.
Console output is the product of a tooling script, not a stray debug left in shipped code. Reaches these packages only through their own build/lint config files.
An empty block is how a no-op stub is spelled — `vi.fn(() => {})` and empty catch blocks that assert a throw was swallowed. Repo-wide for test files.
Shadowing an outer binding inside a mock or fixture factory is idiomatic in test code and reads more clearly than inventing a second name. Off for every test file in the repo, not for these packages.
The rule protects Fast Refresh, which never runs in a test file. A suite legitimately exports helpers and fixtures alongside a test component.
A fixture renders a fixed id on purpose so the assertion can find it; uniqueness across a suite is neither achievable nor meaningful. Repo-wide for test files.
The TSX half of the same test-file exemption for no-op stubs.
The TSX half of the same test-file exemption; the two globs exist because Biome matches on the literal extension.
The TSX half of the same Fast-Refresh exemption; ADR-007 barrels are unaffected because the rule stays on for source files.
The TSX half of the same fixed-id fixture exemption, and the one that actually fires — most rendering tests are TSX.
Config fragments kept in a config/ directory follow the same default-export contract as the top-level config files.
Same reasoning as the .mjs glob, for scripts written in TypeScript. noConsole stays on for all other source in every workspace.

Cannot be correct in this monorepo. The shared ESLint config resolves its plugins from the consuming workspace via fromWorkspace(name), a dynamic import by string, so each React workspace must declare typescript-eslint, @stylexjs/eslint-plugin and globals even though nothing in its own source imports them. They are load-bearing; removing one breaks the ESLint pass. Genuine unused dependencies are still caught by fallow. Off repo-wide, not for these packages.

The rule does not apply to a Vite repo, and its own documentation says so: it names Vite tree-shaking as the false-positive case. Verified here rather than assumed — an entry importing one symbol from a flagged barrel builds to that symbol alone, with the barrel module elided. Acting on it would also contradict ADR-007, which requires importing through a curated barrel across a module boundary. Off repo-wide, not for these packages.

approved.reason: A column resize handle is a window splitter: role=separator with keyboard resize semantics. HTML has no native element carrying that role, so Biome's suggested substitution has nothing to substitute.

A virtualization spacer row is decorative by construction: it renders one empty colSpan'd cell, declares no role and carries no tabIndex, so no focusable descendant exists and aria-hidden is correct. Biome flags aria-hidden on any table row because inside a role=grid a row IS focusable — which the Table now is (ADR-062) — and it cannot see that this particular row opts out of the grid's row sequence entirely.

`<table role="grid">` is the WAI-ARIA APG's own markup for an interactive data grid, and here the role is not an upgrade of an implicit one: TableBody.stylex.ts makes the populated <tbody> a CSS grid, so the browser drops the implicit table roles and this attribute is their only source. Biome's rule maps role to element without modelling that; jsx-a11y, the upstream it ports, ships `table: ['grid']` as a default allowance on the same rule. Its suggested fix (drop the role, or use a div) restores the bug ADR-062 exists to close.

Same mapping, one level down: `<td role="gridcell">` is the APG's cell markup, and TableBodyCell.stylex.ts sets every body cell to `display: flex`, which is what removes the implicit `cell` role. jsx-a11y ships `td: ['gridcell']` as a default allowance on this rule; Biome's port carries no options at all, so the file is the only available scope.

Identical to the TableRow case, for the header cell: a <th> inside a `display: flex` row loses its implicit `columnheader` role, so the explicit one is the only source of it and of the `aria-sort` announcement that hangs off it. `scope="col"` is declared alongside because it is correct markup, and is what narrows Biome's complaint from useSemanticElements to this rule.

The role is redundant only if the element still has its implicit one. TableRow.stylex.ts sets every <tr> to `display: flex`, and a browser drops an element's implicit table role along with its table `display` — so `role="row"` is the grid's only row semantics, not a duplicate. The rule reads JSX; the fact that makes the attribute load-bearing is in the stylesheet. Deleting it, as the rule suggests, breaks the row/cell ownership `role="grid"` requires.

The APG tabs pattern requires the tabpanel itself be focusable so keyboard users reach panel content after the tab strip. tabIndex on a non-interactive element is exactly what the pattern prescribes here, not an oversight.

The trigger adds role=button and tabIndex only when its child is not already natively interactive, so the handlers always sit on something focusable at runtime. Biome evaluates the JSX statically and cannot follow the conditional role.

A default export IS the ESLint rule API — `ESLintUtils.RuleCreator` returns the rule module and the plugin registry imports each one as default, so every rule file must have one. This is the same contract already acknowledged repo-wide for config modules, scoped to a package rather than an extension because that is where rule modules live. Narrowed from the whole package to `src/` when @lcabrera/eslint-plugin became public.

Console output is this module's entire function — it is the single sanctioned wrapper every other module routes through, which is what lets noConsole stay on everywhere else. The glob resolves to exactly one file, packages/ui/src/utils/logger/logger.util.ts.

React Compiler owns memoization in this repo, so hand-maintained dependency arrays are deliberately absent. Biome's rule demands the exact thing ADR-004 removed; leaving it on would flag correct code across the whole package.
Same prototype save-and-restore as mockDialogElement, applied to the popover API methods this suite stubs. Binding breaks restoration for the same reason.

CSS anchor positioning (anchor-name, position-anchor, position-area) is a shipped browser feature that StyleX's property allowlist predates. Verified still load-bearing on 2026-07-22: deleting the directives produces 6 real eslint errors.
Same CSS anchor positioning gap as TooltipContent — StyleX cannot validate a property its allowlist does not yet contain, and the anchor name is what binds trigger to content.

Saves HTMLDialogElement prototype methods so teardown can restore them. Binding them, as the rule wants, produces new function identities and the restore silently stops restoring. Spelled oxlint-disable because only Oxlint recognises the typescript-eslint/ prefix.
